para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether the ``.ini`` file carries anything to remap. ``false`` for a file that only WATCHES the character -- eg. a help overlay whose one section matches the position hash to know she is on screen, which remapped like a mod would draw a second copy of her :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: ``true``

parameterdescription.para: Whether the file carries anything to remap

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether the ``.ini`` file is a RECOLOUR and nothing else: it draws none of the character's mesh, no other ``.ini`` file beside it does, and it overrides a texture of the character that the target does not draw. Its whole model then comes from downloads, with the mod's textures bound in place of the downloaded ones -- so a fixer that reads the mod's buffers while it is being built has to fetch those downloads first :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: ``false``

parameterdescription.para: Whether the file is a recolour and nothing else

para.verbatim:
embed:rst `Sections`_ a fix writes into every ``.ini`` file it generates, so a SIBLING's toggle keeps working there: a ``[Constants]`` declaring a copy of each variable a carried recolour's condition reads, and a copy of each sibling ``[Key...]`` section that cycles one, both under the copy's name :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A file with no ``namespace =`` is named after its PATH, so a variable of one ``.ini`` cannot be read from another. The copy is driven by the same key under the same condition, so the two keep in step :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: empty -- nothing to carry
embed:rst Whether the mod leaves a mod object UNDRAWN -- on its own character the game never draws it, so a fix must not draw a download of it over the mod's own buffers

briefdescription.para: Records that the mod leaves 'modObj' undrawn.
Forgets every mod object addUndrawn recorded.
Every mod object the mod leaves undrawn.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The draws the mod's own `sections`_ of a mod object make with numbers, in the order they are written -- not ``drawindexed = auto``, which draws the whole of whatever is bound

embed:rst Which parts of the mod object's `sections`_ hold a ``drawindexed``, counted from 1 over every part of a `section`_ (an ``if`` line is a part too). Draws all in one part are draws under one condition

embed:rst The texture registers a mod object's `sections`_ bind only AFTER they have drawn, in the order first bound. A draw before them renders with whatever the game had bound, so a mod whose section draws, then binds, then draws again has two binding generations

embed:rst Whether the mod replaces a game texture BY HASH anywhere -- a texture override with a ``hash`` and a ``this =`` -- so its art reaches every draw that binds that texture, whatever the draw's own `section`_ binds

embed:rst The ``filename =`` of one of the mod's resource `sections`_, found without regard to the case of its name, or ``std::nullopt``. The value is the ``.ini``'s own (a Windows path, relative to the ``.ini``)

briefdescription.para: Every resource section_ of the mod that names a file, as lowercased name -> filename.

para.verbatim: embed:rst What role each texture of the ``.ini`` plays, or ``nullptr`` when the parser records none -- every role the ``.ini`` binds a file for, since one atlas can serve two objects

embed:rst Fills the texture data -- #textureRoles, #roleCandidates, #roleFile, #rejections -- on the first ask of any of them, rather than now :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Sorting a mod's textures may open every one of them, and a parser is built for every ``.ini`` a run classifies, most of which no fixer asks about

parameterdescription.para: What fills them, or empty for nothing

parameterdescription.para: Why, as a sentence about the file

para.verbatim:
embed:rst What a parser learned about a ``.ini`` file that a fixer needs and cannot read off the sections it is handed -- the classification data a parser keeps, whatever the game :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Every :cpp:class:`BaseIniParser` owns one (:cpp:func:`BaseIniParser::parseData`): the parser fills it while it parses, and a fixer reads it through the parser it is given. A parser that fills nothing leaves the defaults, which say "everything is there": the file has something to remap, no mod object is undrawn, and no texture has a known role :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A mod object is ``(component, object)``, as the parser's graphs are keyed -- eg. ``("Body", "C")`` for a slot of a GI component, ``("", "component3")`` for a Wuthering Waves draw slot :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` What the mod's textures ARE comes in three layers, each read off the one before: which roles each file plays (#textureRoles), the candidates left for each role once the files that cannot serve it are refused (#roleCandidates, #rejections), and the one file each mod object takes for a role (#roleFile). The expensive ones may be filled on the first ask -- see #defer
